classes.name: Storage
classes.summary:
{@link Storage | `Storage`} package is used to write and read persistent objects. These objects are read and written by a retrieval or storage algorithm ({@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} object) in a container (disk, memory, network ...). Drivers (`FSD_File` objects) assign a physical container for data to be stored or retrieved. The standard procedure for an application in reading a container is the following:
- open the driver in reading mode,
- call the Read function from the schema, setting the driver as a parameter. This function returns an instance of the {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} class which contains the data being read,
- close the driver. The standard procedure for an application in writing a container is the following:
- open the driver in writing mode,
- create an instance of the {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} class, then add the persistent data to write with the function AddRoot,
- call the function Write from the schema, setting the driver and the {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} instance as parameters,
- close the driver.

staticMethods.name: Version
staticMethods.comment: returns the version of {@link Storage | `Storage`}'s read/write routines

classes.name: Storage_Data
classes.summary:
A picture memorizing the data stored in a container (for example, in a file). A {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object represents either:
- persistent data to be written into a container, or
- persistent data which are read from a container. A {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object is used in both the storage and retrieval operations:
- {@link Storage | `Storage`} mechanism: create an empty {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object, then add successively persistent objects (roots) to be stored using the function AddRoot. When the set of data is complete, write it to a container using the function Write in your {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} storage/retrieval algorithm.
- Retrieval mechanism: a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object is returned by the Read function from your {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} storage/retrieval algorithm. Use the functions NumberOfRoots and Roots to find the roots which were stored in the read container. The roots of a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object may share references on objects. The shared internal references of a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object are maintained by the storage/retrieval mechanism.
Note: References shared by objects which are contained in two distinct {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} objects are not maintained by the storage/retrieval mechanism: external references are not supported by {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} algorithm

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.comment: Creates an empty set of data. You explicitly create a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object when preparing the set of objects to be stored together in a container (for example, in a file). Then use the function AddRoot to add persistent objects to the set of data. A {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object is also returned by the Read function of a {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} storage/retrieval algorithm. Use the functions NumberOfRoots and Roots to find the roots which were stored in the read container.

instanceMethods.name: ErrorStatus
instanceMethods.comment:
Returns Storage_VSOk if.
- the last storage operation performed with the function Read, or
- the last retrieval operation performed with the function Write by a {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} algorithm, on this set of data was successful. If the storage or retrieval operation was not performed, the returned error status indicates the reason why the operation failed. The algorithm stops its analysis at the first detected error

instanceMethods.name: ClearErrorStatus
instanceMethods.comment:
Clears the error status positioned either by:
- the last storage operation performed with the Read function, or
- the last retrieval operation performed with the Write function by a {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} algorithm, on this set of data. This error status may be read by the function ErrorStatus.

instanceMethods.name: NumberOfRoots
instanceMethods.comment:
Returns the number of root objects in this set of data.
- When preparing a storage operation, the result is the number of roots inserted into this set of data with the function AddRoot.
- When retrieving an object, the result is the number of roots stored in the read container. Use the Roots function to get these roots in a sequence.

instanceMethods.name: AddRoot
instanceMethods.comment: add a persistent root to write. the name of the root is a driver reference number.

instanceMethods.name: AddRoot
instanceMethods.comment: Adds the root anObject to this set of data. The name of the root is aName if given; if not, it will be a reference number assigned by the driver when writing the set of data into the container. When naming the roots, it is easier to retrieve objects by significant references rather than by references without any semantic values.

instanceMethods.name: RemoveRoot
instanceMethods.comment: Removes from this set of data the root object named aName. Warning Nothing is done if there is no root object whose name is aName in this set of data.

instanceMethods.name: Roots
instanceMethods.comment:
Returns the roots of this set of data in a sequence.
- When preparing a storage operation, the sequence contains the roots inserted into this set of data with the function AddRoot.
- When retrieving an object, the sequence contains the roots stored in the container read.
- An empty sequence is returned if there is no root in this set of data.

instanceMethods.comment: Gives the root object whose name is aName in this set of data. The returned object is a {@link Storage_Root | `Storage_Root`} object, from which the object it encapsulates may be extracted. classes.name: Storage_Root
classes.summary:
A root object extracted from a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object.
A {@link Storage_Root | `Storage_Root`} encapsulates a persistent object which is a root of a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object. It contains additional information: the name and the data type of the persistent object.
When retrieving a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object from a container (for example, a file) you access its roots with the function Roots which returns a sequence of root objects. The provided functions allow you to request information about each root of the sequence.
You do not create explicit roots: when inserting data in a {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object, you just provide the persistent object and optionally its name to the function AddRoot.

instanceMethods.name: Name
instanceMethods.comment:
Returns the name of this root object.
The name may have been given explicitly when the root was inserted into the {@link Storage_Data | `Storage_Data`} object.
If not, the name is a reference number which was assigned automatically by the driver when writing the set of data into the container.
When naming the roots, it is easier to retrieve objects by significant references rather than by references without any semantic values.
Warning The returned string will be empty if you call this function before having named this root object, either explicitly, or when writing the set of data into the container.

instanceMethods.name: Object
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the persistent object encapsulated by this root.

instanceMethods.name: Type
instanceMethods.comment: Returns the name of this root type.

instanceMethods.name: AddRoot
instanceMethods.comment: add a root to <me>. If a root with same name is present, it will be replaced by <aRoot>.

instanceMethods.name: Find
instanceMethods.comment: find a root with name <aName>.

instanceMethods.name: IsRoot
instanceMethods.comment: returns true if <me> contains a root named <aName>

instanceMethods.name: RemoveRoot
instanceMethods.comment: remove the root named <aName>.

classes.name: Storage_Schema
classes.summary:
Root class for basic storage/retrieval algorithms. A {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} object processes:
- writing of a set of persistent data into a container (store mechanism),
- reading of a container to extract all the contained persistent data (retrieve mechanism). A {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} object is based on the data schema for the persistent data of the application, i.e.:
- the list of all persistent objects which may be known by the application,
- the organization of their data; a data schema knows how to browse each persistent object it contains.
During the store or retrieve operation, only persistent objects known from the data schema can be processed; they are then stored or retrieved according to their description in the schema. A data schema is specific to the object classes to be read or written.
Tools dedicated to the environment in use allow a description of the application persistent data structure. {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} algorithms are called basic because they do not support external references between containers.

constructors.name: constructor
constructors.comment:
Builds a storage/retrieval algorithm based on a given data schema. Example For example, if ShapeSchema is the class inheriting from {@link Storage_Schema | `Storage_Schema`} and containing the description of your application data schema, you create a storage/retrieval algorithm as follows: `occ::handle<ShapeSchema>` s = new ShapeSchema;.
USER API - -------------------------------------------------------------

staticMethods.name: CheckTypeMigration
staticMethods.comment:
returns True if theType migration is identified the callback support provides a way to read a file with a incomplete schema. ex. A file contains 3 types a, b, and c. The application's schema contains only 2 type a and b. If you try to read the file in the application, you will have an error. To bypass this problem you can give to your application's schema a callback used when the schema doesn't know how to handle this type.
@param theNewName Mutated in place; read the updated value from this argument after the call.
